question: Which temple, built by the Chandela dynasty in the 10th-11th centuries, is known for its exquisite sculptures?
solution:
The correct answer is __**Kandariya Mahadeva Temple**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• The Kandariya Mahadeva Temple is one of the largest and most ornate Hindu temples in the medieval temple group of Khajuraho, located in Madhya Pradesh, India.
 
• It was built during the reign of King Vidyadhara of the Chandela dynasty in the 10th-11th centuries.
 
• The temple is dedicated to Lord Shiva and derives its name "Kandariya" from the Sanskrit word meaning "cave" or "mountain," symbolizing Mount Kailash, Lord Shiva's abode.
 
• It is renowned for its intricate sculptures and carvings, which depict various aspects of life, including deities, celestial beings, and scenes of daily life.
 
• The Kandariya Mahadeva Temple is part of the UNESCO World Heritage Site of Khajuraho, famous for its architectural brilliance and erotic sculptures.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Chandela Dynasty:** The Chandela dynasty ruled central India between the 9th and 13th centuries and is known for its patronage of art and architecture, particularly the Khajuraho Group of Monuments.
 
• **Khajuraho Group of Monuments:** This site comprises 85 temples at its peak, with only 22 surviving today, and is divided into three groups: western, eastern, and southern.
 
• **Nagara Style Architecture:** The Kandariya Mahadeva Temple is an exemplary example of Nagara-style architecture, characterized by a curvilinear shikhara (spire) and intricate ornamentation.
 
• **Erotic Sculptures:** The temple features sculptures with sensual and erotic themes, which symbolize the Tantric traditions and the celebration of life and human emotions.
 
• **UNESCO World Heritage Site:** The Khajuraho temples were inscribed as a UNESCO World Heritage Site in 1986, recognizing their cultural and artistic significance.
